messages.author: 93c2c8c16675e403
messages.subject: Setting xlimits in ggplot (hopefully automatically)
parts:
Hi all

How does one set x and y limits on a graph? ...

Attached is an example graph, with icky limits -- they should be
"[15,20)" on the left, and "[50, 55)" on the right. There is a lot of
NaN data because we are graphing fertility rates for women, so my data
source (ACS PUMS) puts NAs in this variable whenever the variable
doesn't apply, like to women between 15 and 45 (if you disagree, take
it up with the Bureau not me...) I would like to calculate where the
NA's start and stop and only graph in between. I don't want different
size data.frames for other reasons.

Here is the code I am using to graph:

g = ggplot() + layer(data = ratesdf, mapping = aes(x = age, y = rate,
group=group), geom = "point", stat="identity") + layer(data = ratesdf,
mapping = aes(x = age, y = rate, group=1), geom = "smooth", stat =
"smooth", method = loess)

Here is the data (the "[0,5)" thing for age is an ordered factor
result of cut() ):

$ratesdf
rate age group
[0,5) NaN [0,5) g1
[5,10) NaN [5,10) g1
[10,15) NaN [10,15) g1
[15,20) 0.08658690 [15,20) g1
[20,25) 0.19596098 [20,25) g1
[25,30) 0.16773879 [25,30) g1
[30,35) 0.15077417 [30,35) g1
[35,40) 0.06739765 [35,40) g1
[40,45) 0.03144191 [40,45) g1
[45,50) 0.00000000 [45,50) g1
[50,55) 0.00000000 [50,55) g1
[55,60) NaN [55,60) g1
[60,65) NaN [60,65) g1
[65,70) NaN [65,70) g1
[70,75) NaN [70,75) g1
[75,80) NaN [75,80) g1
[80,85) NaN [80,85) g1
[85,Inf] NaN [85,Inf] g1

Any help is appreciated!

messages.author: e53f91d0708becab
messages.subject: Re: Setting xlimits in ggplot (hopefully automatically)
parts:
There is more than one option but this should work

ratesdf<-ratesdf[!is.na(ratesdf$rate),]

ratesdf<-as.data.frame(lapply(ratesdf, function(x) x[,drop=TRUE]))
